topics.label: Welcome and Lecture Framing
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture themes, learning outcomes, and foundational concepts regarding cancer evolution and the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Clonal Selection and Epigenetic Plasticity in Cancer Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how cancer progression is driven by the Darwinian selection of fitter mutated clones alongside non-mutational epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Cell Hierarchy and Stem Cell Origins in Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the cancer stem cell model and investigate whether malignancies initiate within tissue-specific stem cells or through dedifferentiation across hematopoietic and intestinal tissues.

topics.label: Microenvironmental Promotion and Inflammatory Signaling in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: They demonstrate how external promoters and inflammatory microenvironmental stimuli provide the necessary secondary signals to drive mutated cells into malignant growth.

topics.label: Established Microenvironments, Spatial Profiling, and Coevolutionary Synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the stromal dependencies of established tumors, the experimental technologies used to profile spatial heterogeneity, and the broader synthesis of cancer as a coevolutionary process between cells and their environment.

topics.label: Closing Remarks and Next Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the session and announces the subject of the upcoming lecture.
